title: Fleet Recall / Requests
description: MCP and HTTP operational traffic, terminal outcomes, latency, concurrency and protocol health. Request boundaries remain separate; metrics contain fixed labels only.

options.content:
**MCP and HTTP are separate measurement boundaries.** Do not add their totals: a remote HTTP handler can contain an MCP dispatch for the same request. MCP includes tool calls, protocol requests, rejected frames, and skipped one-way notifications; use **Operation** to narrow it.

**Deployment** and **Instance** filter the entire dashboard. **Operation** filters MCP panels only. Rates use the adaptive scrape window; totals cover the selected time range. **No samples** means a series has not been observed, not that its value is zero. Use the Overview to check target availability.

panels.title: Completed / second
panels.description: All terminal MCP observations for the selected operations, including rejected frames and skipped notifications. A request contributes exactly one MCP terminal outcome.

panels.title: Backend errors / second
panels.description: Outcome=error: MCP isError results and internal failures. Refusals, invalid requests, deadlines, and caller cancellations are separate outcomes.

panels.title: Refused / second
panels.description: Typed service refusals with not_applied outcomes. These are intentional policy or lifecycle decisions; inspect sanitized operation.completed events for context.

panels.title: Invalid / second
panels.description: Malformed envelopes, invalid parameters, unsupported methods or actions, and rejected frames. This is distinct from backend failure.

panels.title: Timed out / second
panels.description: The MCP stdio request deadline expired. An interrupted mutation may have an unknown commit outcome; a timeout is not proof of rollback.

panels.title: In flight
panels.description: Current MCP dispatches still executing, summed across selected instances and operations. A stable nonzero value should be interpreted with latency and traffic.

panels.title: Traffic by operation
panels.description: Terminal observations per second. Protocol operations and notifications are included when selected; use recall.* and remember.* operation values to inspect tool traffic.

panels.title: Outcomes over time
panels.description: One terminal outcome per MCP observation. Cancelled means the caller or enclosing future stopped waiting; it does not imply a mutation was rolled back.

panels.title: Concurrent dispatches by operation
panels.description: Instantaneous in-flight gauge. Connections waiting for a new stdio frame are not dispatches and do not count here.

panels.title: Outcomes in the selected range
panels.description: Estimated terminal counts from increase() over the dashboard time range. Counter resets are handled; scrape-boundary extrapolation can produce fractional estimates. An absent outcome remains no data.

panels.title: MCP  /  latency distribution and operation detail
p50 duration by operation
panels.description: Histogram estimate across selected instances, grouped by operation. Includes all terminal outcomes, including failure, timeout and cancellation. With no recent observations, quantiles remain no data.

panels.title: p95 duration by operation
panels.description: Histogram estimate across selected instances, grouped by operation. Includes all terminal outcomes, including failure, timeout and cancellation. With no recent observations, quantiles remain no data. The 2-second guide matches the example MCP latency alert; the alert also requires sufficient traffic and sustained duration.

panels.title: p99 duration by operation
panels.description: Histogram estimate across selected instances, grouped by operation. Includes all terminal outcomes, including failure, timeout and cancellation. With no recent observations, quantiles remain no data.

panels.title: Duration distribution
panels.description: Completed MCP durations across the selected operations. Prometheus heatmap formatting converts cumulative le buckets into non-overlapping buckets; cell intensity is operations per second. All outcomes are included. Select one operation to inspect its distribution.

panels.title: Operation × outcome · selected range
panels.description: Estimated completed observations per operation and outcome in the selected time range. This table includes only measured series; no rows are manufactured for unseen outcomes.

panels.title: Rejected frames and protocol requests
panels.description: Invalid UTF-8 and oversized frames, parse/envelope failures, unknown methods, and unknown tool/actions. Labels are fixed categories; raw method names and request contents never enter these metrics. The Operation selector also applies here.

panels.title: Skipped notifications
panels.description: Notifications are one-way and intentionally ignored. Notification-shaped tools/call messages do not execute a hidden mutation. This chart reflects protocol bookkeeping, not successful tool work; selecting other operations leaves it empty.

options.content:
These panels cover the implemented **http_demo** and **http_ingress** surfaces. The MCP **Operation** selector does not filter HTTP routes. Routing, limits, and authentication failures are measured at the HTTP boundary.

HTTP outcomes describe the handler response; they do not determine the outcome of a nested MCP tool call. Response-class counts require a produced response, while outcome counts also include cancelled handlers. HTTP duration ends when the handler returns a response; it does not measure client download time.

panels.title: HTTP traffic by surface and route
panels.description: Terminal HTTP handler observations, including rejections. Current demo categories are index, health, status and recall; webhook requests use ingress. Unmatched or unsupported route patterns remain other.

panels.title: HTTP terminal outcomes
panels.description: 401/403/429 are refused; 408/504 are timeout; remaining 4xx are invalid; 5xx are error. A cancelled handler may not have produced an HTTP response.

panels.title: HTTP response classes
panels.description: Produced responses by status class and HTTP surface. These counters exclude handlers cancelled before producing a response. A 2xx HTTP response is not evidence that a nested MCP tool succeeded.

panels.title: HTTP p95 by surface and route
panels.description: Handler duration estimated from histograms. Aggregation keeps HTTP surface and route categories separate; body download time is outside this measurement boundary.

panels.title: HTTP handlers in flight
panels.description: Handlers currently executing, grouped by HTTP surface and route. This does not count open idle connections.

panels.title: HTTP outcomes · selected range
panels.description: Estimated terminal HTTP observations per surface and outcome over the selected time range. Keep these totals separate from MCP totals. Absent series are not converted to zero.
